title: AI spy options Agent (work in progress)
author: Reasonable_Comb3171
selftext: I’ve been developing an agent that trades stock options on the SPY, so far so good it’s in freeze for the next month while I collect results from real time trades. I’m hesitant to run a test on the past 20 days with the agent because I fear there will be future leakage that will influence its trade decisions. Not enough time has passed to tell if it’s hits are strictly luck based. So far though it’s doing a great job saving money by not chasing and when it makes a move the direction is correct it’s just having issues sizing the trade I think that has to do with its infancy at this current time. For example yesterday it bought in and was expecting a 40% return but the option peaked at 27 or so percent so it didn’t engage the profit lock which starts at 30% then trails until it dumps at the target. The model is thesis driven and will look for holes emerging in its thesis while the trade is active when it senses that the winds have switched it has dumped the contract with a gain the other day it saved itself with +7% when it detected the thesis was no longer in tact. I’m posting on here to see if anyone has any advice/ insight. Thank you. The model is currently trading a paper account with alpaca on the free data plan. If results are good after the freeze I’ll look into paying for the better data. I’m using the Claude console API, sonnet and haiku

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: the free Alpaca plan would worry me before the leakage does. option quotes on that tier come from the indicative feed, not the full one, and the paper account fills kinder than a live book would, so a +7% save on a SPY contract can be mostly spread. I ran into that with my own agents, so when I built Quantradin for AIs trading fake money I made every option buy pay the ask and every sale take the bid. quantradin.com. what expiry is it buying, same day or a few days out?

replies.author: Reasonable_Comb3171
replies.body: Right now it’s day trading options that expire tomorrow or today it depends on its risk assessment and if the move is going to take minutes versus an hour or more. It can go long as well. the agent sizes the option contact for the move it feels is going to occur based on its live news analysis and its understanding of the trend. There is a confidence score, right now the model determines its own confidence it’s not based on any static criteria but at the same time I’m having the agent note not act on information that it passes through a static baseline for a 0/7 confidence test to be evaluated at the end of freeze week 4. I’m really just using this as an opportunity to learn more about how I can use Claude and AI agents as a whole in general. I’m not convinced of anything. I do want to get the data plan because of what you said, at least these spy options it’s trading are incredibly liquid in terms of the spread.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: same-day and next-day contracts are where a paper fill flatters most, the spread can widen a lot in the minute after a headline, which is when your agent wants in. I'd log bid and ask at every entry and exit so the run can be re-priced at the worst side later. and score that confidence number against outcomes before it sizes anything.

comments.author: Due_Set_6523
comments.body:
nice project. i think you’re right to skip the backtest but for a different reason. sonnet/haiku were trained on recent market data so they might already “know” how those days went lol. forward testing is the cleaner way imo

on the 27% vs 40% thing, i’d look at the exit before the sizing. if the lock only kicks in at 30% it does nothing on a trade that tops out at 27 and dumps. maybe scale out a bit earlier?

replies.author: Reasonable_Comb3171
replies.body: That’s the one thing I decided to modify I changed it to lock in at 0% when it hits 25 then it trails. This felt like it wasn’t going to severely offset my results especially since it’s only week one. Aside from that one change I’m letting it all ride for the next 4 weeks. I saw that about sonnet and haiku. I was also thinking that since it has to download the option pricing for the test itself and it only downloads within x amount of contracts within the price of the SPY i assumed it might be able to trace where price is going by how many contracts are available to pick from.

replies.author: Due_Set_6523
replies.body:
oh breakeven at 25 then trail makes a lot of sense, way safer than waiting for 30. i’d just note the day you changed it so you can compare before vs after at the end

and yeah good catch on the contracts thing. if the backtest pulls the chain as it looks now and not as it looked on that day, the strikes that are listed could give away where price ended up. so if you ever do backtest, make sure the data is a snapshot from that exact time

replies.author: Reasonable_Comb3171
replies.body: Thank goodness for Claude I’ve got everything written up in a log. I’m trying to be very careful with it the results over the last couple days were favorable. Still tells no difference between its results actually being true versus a coin flip. I’m having Claude code summarize and log each days results within the agent to identify if any issues are making themselves known and how we can go about fixing them after the freeze. I’m learning a lot it’s fascinating
